subject: Retention exception for customer sandbox — proposed timeline and subprocessor notes
messages:
From: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@medrx.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Compliance Team <compliance@medrx.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term hold on sandbox backups + log window for audit

Rachel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our auditors asked for an operational clarification around the sandbox environment we use for integration testing with Redwood. Two asks: 1) can Redwood hold sandbox backups for an additional 60 days (instead of our default 30) for the period June 15–Sept 15 so we can complete a retrospective audit? 2) can logs associated with those sandbox runs be retained for 90 days (they default to 30) to cover cross-team traceability?

We realize this is a temporary change and are happy to sign any narrow scoped amendment that makes the exception auditable and time-boxed. Please advise what information you need from us (POC, evidence requirements, acceptance criteria) and whether any subprocessor cross-border notifications are required.

— Aaron
Aaron Patel
Head of Integrations, MedRx Health
aaron.patel@medrx.com
+1 415 555 0123

From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term hold on sandbox backups + log window for audit

Aaron —

Appreciate the clear ask and the timeline. High-level response and next steps from our side:

- We can do a temporary retention increase for sandbox backups and logs with these constraints: the window must be explicitly time-limited, Redwood will produce an auditable manifest of the retained snapshots, and the increased retention must be scoped to named sandboxes (not production).

- Options to meet your needs: (A) Increase sandbox backup retention to 60 days and log retention to 90 days for the requested period (June 15–Sept 15). (B) Keep the standard retention but run a scheduled export/escrow snapshot for any runs you want preserved for audit (we can deliver a single encrypted export to MedRx S3).

- Operational impacts: longer retention will delay purge by up to 30 days and will count against your data retention quota for the account during the window. There is also a minor uptick in token and storage billing for the retained snapshots.

Action items I propose:
1) MedRx confirms PII/data categories in scope and which sandboxes to include (reply with sandbox IDs).
2) Redwood legal to issue a narrow DPA amendment / annex (karthik, can you draft a one-page amendment we can route for signature?).
3) Ops to prepare a manifest and export cadence; we can also provide a single escrow export if preferred (laura, can you prepare the export options matrix?).
4) Confirm whether any of the retained data will be subject to cross-border transfer (Aaron, note yes/no and where your auditors are located).

I'll hold off on changing policies until we have the signed amendment or a mutual action plan. Copying Soojin (security) and Karthik (legal) to drive the DPA note.

Thanks —
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Manager, Customer Ops — Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
Attachment: proposed-retention-exception-2028-06.xlsx (xlsx)
From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@medrx.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2028 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term hold on sandbox backups + log window for audit

Aaron / Rachel —

I can take the DPA annex. Proposed approach: a 1-page appendix to the existing DPA that (a) enumerates sandbox IDs and dates for the temporary exception, (b) defines retention windows (backups = 60 days, logs = 90 days), (c) includes an auditable manifest requirement and encrypted export option, and (d) auto-expires on 2028-09-16. For cross-border transfers: if any sandbox data moves outside the US we will flag subprocessors and add an addendum to the subprocessor list with timestamps.

Question for MedRx: are you requesting any changes to our subprocessor authorization flow (i.e., pre-approval for the list for this window) or is a post-facto notification sufficient? If you want pre-approval we need ~3 business days to process and an update to the annex.

I'll start drafting and will post a DocuSign link once the team vets the language.

— Karthik
Head of Legal Ops, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@medrx.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2028 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term hold on sandbox backups + log window for audit

Aaron —

From a security and compliance standpoint I have two recommendations that minimize risk:

1) Scope the exception to named sandbox IDs and a single customer-owned S3 export option. That limits our exposure and avoids any cross-customer contamination.

2) If MedRx has European auditors accessing sandbox artifacts, we should avoid allowing backups to be moved to non-EU datacenters for that data. For cross-border cases we recommend using our Private VPC connector or a customer-managed export; we can also flag subprocessors that would touch the export.

Operational note: we will enable audit-level logging for every export and produce the manifest with checksums. We will require a signed annex or an explicit email approval from an authorized MedRx signatory before we enact the retention change.

Let us know the sandbox IDs and whether you prefer the escrow export or the extended retention.

— Soojin
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Team —

Thanks — MedRx prefers option B: perform a single encrypted escrow export for the selected runs and keep the platform policy at standard retention. That will make the audit simpler for us and reduces cross-customer risk on your side. We will provide the list of sandbox IDs by EOD tomorrow and confirm whether any auditors are overseas (likely two in UK).

We are happy to proceed with the DPA annex as described. Please share the DocuSign link and the export options matrix so we can pick (S3 export to our bucket vs SCP transfer to our secure staging host).

Best —
Aaron
